note: The gnu6-design sheet bound its own roles by hand: thirty-four of them,
for the dark substrate and for the light one, in two :root blocks. That is
a hand-made role layer, and it is where the sheet's colours that the
system does not have came from.
This is the binding the system publishes, expressed in the sheet's own
variable names. Each colour the sheet declared is bound to the step of the
system that carries it, so the sheet names the system instead of carrying
The family decides the hue and the sheet's own lightness decides the step,
which is the rule the surface layer is built on. Three of the bindings are
judgements rather than a nearest step, and they say so.

judgements.why: The light substrate's link hover was a blue darker than the system's darkest blue step. The system owns the blue, so the link takes its base and the hover takes the 700 step: the affordance the sheet had - the hover moves away from the substrate - is preserved, and the system's base is the system's canonical blue.

The light substrate's action hover was a navy tint of the strong ink. The system's step is a neutral one, so the hover becomes a neutral lift rather than a blue one. The system's neutral is the system's.

The middle ink of the light substrate. The system's light ink ramp began at 0.445 and its strong ink was at 0.14, so there was a hole in the coverage and the field's converged value fell into it. The step was added to the ramp, and this is where it was already wanted.
